root.name: Alekhine Defense: The Squirrel
root.moves: 1. e4 Nf6 2. e5 Nd5 3. c4 Nf4

overview: After 1.e4 Nf6 2.e5 Nd5 3.c4 Black's knight jumps to f4, hitting g2 and d3 at the cost of time. White normally replies 4.d4 and later d4 d6 ideas, keeping a space edge. I am not sure of the precise lines; the knight tends to be harassed with d4, Bxf4 and similar.

white_ideas.idea: Build a centre with d4 and Nc3
Trap or chase the knight on f4 with Bxf4 or Nf3

black_ideas.idea: Use the knight to harass g2 and d3

typical_structures.structure: Alekhine centre with White pawns on e5, d4, c4

character.notes: Concrete tactics around g2 and the knight.

soundness.notes: The Squirrel is not considered fully sound.

structure.notes: White space and centre against Black piece play.

approach.notes: Rare sub-line, almost unplayed at the top.

character.reason: The knight raid creates concrete tactics.

soundness.reason: The knight loses time and strong players avoid it.
